hook_text: Sodium starts with S. Its symbol is Na. Potassium starts with P. Its symbol is K. The Periodic Table is not broken; it is speaking Latin.
clip_script: Look at the sodium box on the Periodic Table. Name: sodium. Symbol: Na. Why? Because the symbol comes from its old Latin name, natrium. Potassium is K from kalium, iron is Fe from ferrum, gold is Au from aurum, and lead is Pb from plumbum, which is why the person who fixes your pipes is called a plumber: pipes used to be made of lead. The rule for every symbol is one capital, or a capital and a small letter. Never two capitals, because CO is not an element; it is carbon monoxide, a deadly gas, while Co is the metal cobalt. Then the number 11 at the top of the box. That is the atomic number, the count of protons in every sodium atom, and it is the element's true identity card. Add one proton and it is not sodium any more; it is magnesium. Names and symbols are labels people chose. The atomic number is nature's.
visual_style: A large whiteboard box for sodium with 11, Na and 23, then Latin names appearing beside Na, K, Fe, Au and Pb; a CO and a Co side by side with a skull icon on CO.
pacing: Quick puzzle, rapid-fire Latin reveals, a firm closing line about the atomic number.
